tool_input.description: Explore ExtendedMessageFormat behavior with scratch program
Check plain MessageFormat toPattern for same literal pattern

result:
Only this one test class exists, and `./_tools/test.sh` (run with no args, so it covers all `*AgentTest.java`) was effectively already exercised above since it's the only one present.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest.java` (JUnit 5 Jupiter, matching the project's existing tests), with 28 self-contained test methods covering construction/locale handling, plain and custom pattern formatting, `toPattern()` round-tripping, registry override of built-in format names, literal/quoted text, error cases (unterminated quote, unterminated format element, invalid/negative argument index), `equals`/`hashCode`, the disabled mutator methods (`setFormat*` throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`), and re-applying a pattern.

27 of 28 tests pass. One fails and demonstrates a real bug:

- **`testCustomFormatNameWithTrailingWhitespaceIsTrimmed`** — the class Javadoc states format-name/format-style values are trimmed of surrounding whitespace, but `ExtendedMessageFormat.getFormat(String)` only trims the name when a style-argument separator (`,`) is present (`src/main/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/ExtendedMessageFormat.java:284-299`). When there's no style argument, trailing whitespace before the closing `}` (e.g. pattern `"{0,upper }"`) is never stripped, so the registry lookup for `"upper "` fails even though `"upper"` is registered. The pattern then falls through to `java.text.MessageFormat`, which also doesn't recognize `"upper "`, and construction throws `IllegalArgumentException: unknown format type: upper`. Leading whitespace (e.g. `"{0, upper}"`) works fine because it's stripped earlier during parsing — only the trailing case is broken.
